title: Flatness of coefficient-model comparison pullback
statement: Let X be a scheme and A any discrete commutative ring in the coefficient universe max(v,u+1). On the recorded etale and pro-etale small site models, the canonical module inverse image constructibleComparisonPullback X A carries every flat module sheaf to a flat module sheaf. No boundedness, constructibility, Noetherian or finite coefficient hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05VD in sites-modules.tex; parent proof step 1.

proof.text: The transported continuous comparison inclusion and canonical constant-section ring map give a ringed-topos morphism with exactly the specified module pushforward. Apply the existing general K-flat pullback theorem and use uniqueness of left adjoints to identify its pullback with constructibleComparisonPullback.

Place the given flat module M in degree zero. All other terms are zero, hence flat. It is bounded above, so it is K-flat. The general pullback theorem gives flat terms for its image. Evaluate in degree zero and transport flatness along the single-complex term isomorphism and the left-adjoint isomorphism.

For any K-flat complex with flat terms, the same supplied ringed-topos theorem gives K-flatness of its termwise pullback. The natural isomorphism of left adjoints induces a complex isomorphism. Tensor it with each acyclic test and transport vanishing homology to the canonical comparison complex.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05VD; proved by applying the supplied ringed-topos K-flat pullback to a flat sheaf in degree zero and using uniqueness of left adjoints.
